item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00029","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C10","C22","C19"],"selected_candidate_label":"C10","confidence":0.74,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C10 is the strongest plausible template because both memoranda reject private relief bills seeking fixed compensation for injuries, proceed from a description of the proposed payment through a detailed account of the injury and available legal remedies, acknowledge the claimant's misfortune, and conclude that the special award lacks sufficient justification under generally applicable law. The shared structure is materially closer than mere veto boilerplate, although the precise grounds differ. C22 has a similar fact-intensive private-claim analysis followed by rejection of making the Government bear losses and a warning about precedent. C19 similarly moves from an apparently equitable individual claim to rejection because approval could invite comparable claims, but its intergovernmental-tax setting is less analogous.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The bill proposed to pay the sums of $5,000 to S. Prather, Junior for personal injuries and property damages","parent_excerpt":"This measure would pay the sum of $10,000 to Harold Joe Davis ... as compensation for alleged permanent disability growing out of injuries sustained","explanation":"Both begin the substantive analysis by identifying a fixed private award and the injuries for which compensation is sought."},{"child_excerpt":"The misfortune suffered by this family ... is most lamentable.","parent_excerpt":"such a bill gives the fullest possible recognition to the equities in favor of the claimant ... [and] the degree of disability he so unfortunately sustained","explanation":"Both expressly recognize the claimant's hardship while distinguishing sympathy or equitable considerations from legal justification for the proposed award."},{"child_excerpt":"Enactment of the bill would constitute a gratuity and would create a dangerous precedent","parent_excerpt":"I find no justification for this proposed award. In amount, it bears no relation to any indicated measure of damages. It constitutes a method of payment which is at variance with the periodic compensation benefits provided by existing law.","explanation":"Both reject an ad hoc lump-sum award because it is not grounded in the ordinary legal framework for determining governmental compensation."},{"child_excerpt":"Accordingly, I am constrained to withhold my approval from the bill.","parent_excerpt":"Accordingly, I am withholding my approval from this bill.","explanation":"The closings are closely parallel, though this is routine veto language and supports the relationship only in combination with the substantive structural parallels."}]}
